post.description: Records an offline payment (cash, cheque, in-kind, other) on a donation form or ticketing campaign, mirroring the dashboard manual-payment flow. Donation forms take an amount; ticketing campaigns take ticket lines (rate ids from GET /campaigns/:id), with amounts and taxes computed server-side. Required custom questions (`questions` in GET /campaigns/:id) are answered in `answers` (buyer) and `tickets[].attendees` (per ticket), such as a membership's member name and email. Auctions are not supported. The payment source is PublicApi.

422.description: The request is well formed but the payment cannot be created on this campaign. `code` says which rule rejected it and `param` names the field it relates to: `campaign_type_not_supported` (`campaign_id`), `payment_method_not_allowed` (`payment_method`), `ticketing_occurrence_is_not_link_to_ticketing` (`occurrence_id`), `tickets_required_for_campaign`, `rate_not_found`, `duplicate_rate_ids`, `pwyc_amount_required`, `amount_not_allowed_for_fixed_rate`, `ticketing_is_full`, `full_choice_errors` (all `tickets`), and `tickets_not_allowed_for_campaign` (whole body). Answers to custom questions are checked against `questions` from GET /campaigns/:id: `missing_required_answers` lists every required question left unanswered with its id, type and choices; `question_not_found`, `question_scope_mismatch` (a `buyer` question under `tickets[].attendees` or the reverse), `choice_not_found` and `invalid_answer` name the faulty answer. Rules shared with the dashboard manual-payment flow, such as a deleted or draft form or an amount outside the accepted range, are reported here too under their own code.

info.title: Zeffy API
info.description:
Public API for accessing Zeffy data — payments, contacts, campaigns, and users.

## Authentication

All requests require a Bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

To get your API key *(organization owner only)*:
1. Go to **[Settings → Integrations](https://www.zeffy.com/o/settings?openIntegrations=true)** in your Zeffy dashboard
2. Create a key and give it a name. Copy it right away: it is shown only once. You can have up to 10 keys and revoke each one separately
3. Use it as: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`

## Errors

Every failing request answers with the same envelope, whatever went wrong:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "resource_not_found",
    "message": "No payment found with id '9f8b7c6d-5e4f-3a2b-1c0d-9e8f7a6b5c4d'.",
    "param": "id",
    "status": 404,
    "doc_url": "https://api.zeffy.com/api/docs"
  }
}
```

`type` tells you which family the failure belongs to, and `code` identifies the exact reason. `param` names the request field at fault when a single one can be blamed, and is `null` otherwise. `status` repeats the HTTP status code.

| `type` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `invalid_request_error` | The request was rejected: bad parameters, missing resource, or a rule that forbids it. |
| `authentication_error` | The API key is missing or invalid. |
| `rate_limit_error` | Too many requests. Wait for the delay in `Retry-After` and retry. |
| `api_error` | Something failed on our side. Retrying later is safe; the `message` is deliberately generic. |

### Error codes

These codes can come back from any endpoint. Codes that belong to a single endpoint are listed on that endpoint.

| `status` | `code` | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_parameters` | A query parameter, a path parameter, or a body field is missing, malformed, or out of range. `message` says which one and `param` names it. An id that is not a UUID reports `param: "id"` and the message `id is not a valid UUID`. |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | The request could not be read at all, for instance a body that is not valid JSON. |
| 401 | `invalid_api_key` | The `Authorization` header is missing, or the bearer token is not a valid API key. |
| 404 | `resource_not_found` | Your organization has no resource of that type with the given id. `param` names the id field at fault. |
| 429 | `rate_limit_exceeded` | You went over one of the rate limits below. |
| 500 | `internal_error` | Something failed on our side. Retrying later is safe. |

## Rate limits

Requests are counted per organization over a sliding window, so every API key of the same organization draws from the same quota. Two windows apply at the same time:

* **100 requests per minute**
* **20 requests per second**, to smooth out bursts

Authenticated responses carry the state of the per-minute window, whether they succeeded or failed:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Requests allowed per minute. |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests left in the current minute. |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp, in seconds, by which the window is guaranteed to have reset. |

A request rejected before authentication (`401`) carries no rate-limit headers, since the quota is tied to your organization. Read these headers when they are there rather than depending on them being there.

Going over either window answers `429` with `rate_limit_exceeded`, plus a `Retry-After` header holding the number of seconds to wait: `60` for the per-minute window, `1` for the burst window.

### Staying under the limits

* Watch `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and slow down before it reaches `0`, rather than waiting for a `429`.
* Keep concurrency in mind: 20 requests per second is the ceiling for the whole organization, not for each of your workers.
* On a `429`, wait for the delay in `Retry-After` before retrying. The window slides, so retrying sooner only spends another rejected request.
* Prefer larger pages (`limit=100`) on the list endpoints, and the `created` filters over re-reading pages you already have. Both move the same data in fewer requests.

Rate limits are not a paid tier, and they are here to keep the API responsive for every organization. If your integration genuinely needs more headroom, please reach out to support and we will look at it with you.

## Webhooks

To receive real-time notifications, configure a webhook URL and pick the events you want in the same **[Integrations dialog](https://www.zeffy.com/o/settings?openIntegrations=true)**.

Your endpoint will receive a `POST` request for each subscribed event. Respond with any `2xx` status to acknowledge receipt — non-2xx responses trigger retries.

| Event | Sent when |
|---|---|
| `payment.completed` | A payment is successfully processed. |
| `payment.created` | A new payment is recorded, whatever its status. |
| `payment.updated` | A payment's status, amount, tip, refunds, dispute, receipt, assigned contact, or assigned fund changes. |
| `payment.deleted` | A payment is deleted. |
| `contact.created` | A new contact is created. |
| `contact.updated` | An editable field on a contact changes. |
| `contact.deleted` | A contact is deleted. |

`*.created` deliveries carry the full resource in `data`. `*.updated` and `*.deleted` deliveries carry an id-only reference in `data` — fetch the resource to read its current state. See each event below for the exact payload.

### Retries

Failed deliveries (non-2xx response or timeout) are retried with an exponential backoff for up to 3 days, over 12 attempts in total. The first retries follow within seconds and minutes, then the gap widens to hours, so a short outage on your side costs you nothing and a long one still leaves you days to recover.

Retry times are jittered, so two events that failed together are not retried at the exact same moment.

If you disable or delete your endpoint, the events still waiting to be retried are abandoned rather than delivered later.

The event `id` in the body stays the same across all attempts: it identifies the event, not the delivery. Use it as an idempotency key to skip events you have already processed.

Each attempt is signed with a fresh timestamp, so the `Zeffy-Signature` value changes between attempts. Always verify the header of the attempt you actually received.

## Webhook signatures

Every webhook delivery includes a `Zeffy-Signature` header that proves the payload comes from Zeffy and was not modified in transit:

```
Zeffy-Signature: t=1700000000,v1=5f5e5d0f7c4c9a3e2b1a0f9e8d7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a2f1e0d9c
```

`t` is the Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the delivery was signed, and `v1` is the hex-encoded `HMAC-SHA256` of the string `{t}.{rawBody}`, keyed with your signing secret.

Your signing secret starts with `whsec_` and is available to organization owners under **Settings → Integrations → Webhook** in the Zeffy dashboard. Keep it private: anyone who knows it can forge valid signatures. If it ever leaks, regenerate it from the same dialog. The previous secret stops working immediately, so update your receiver first.

### Verification steps

1. Read the **raw request body**, before any JSON parsing.
2. Extract `t` and `v1` from the `Zeffy-Signature` header.
3. Compute `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{t}.{rawBody}")` using your signing secret, hex-encoded.
4. Compare it to `v1` with a constant-time comparison (e.g. `crypto.timingSafeEqual` in Node.js).
5. Reject the delivery if `t` is older than your tolerance (we recommend 5 minutes) to prevent replay attacks.

Always verify against the **raw request body bytes**, not a re-serialized version of the parsed JSON: serializers reorder keys and change whitespace, which produces a different signature.

### Node.js example

```js
const crypto = require("crypto");

const TOLERANCE_IN_SECONDS = 5 * 60;

function isZeffySignatureValid(rawBody, signatureHeader, secret) {
  const values = Object.fromEntries(signatureHeader.split(",").map((part) => part.split("=")));
  const timestamp = Number(values.t);
  if (!Number.isFinite(timestamp) || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - timestamp) > TOLERANCE_IN_SECONDS) {
    return false;
  }
  const expected = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${values.t}.${rawBody}`).digest();
  const received = Buffer.from(values.v1 ?? "", "hex");
  return expected.length === received.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(expected, received);
}

// With Express, keep the webhook route on the raw body parser so the bytes stay untouched
app.post("/zeffy-webhook", express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), (request, response) => {
  const isValid = isZeffySignatureValid(
    request.body.toString("utf8"),
    request.get("Zeffy-Signature") ?? "",
    process.env.ZEFFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET
  );
  if (!isValid) {
    return response.status(400).send("Invalid signature");
  }
  const event = JSON.parse(request.body.toString("utf8"));
  // ... handle the event ...
  return response.status(200).send();
});
```

### Python example

```python
import hashlib
import hmac
import time

TOLERANCE_IN_SECONDS = 5 * 60

def is_zeffy_signature_valid(raw_body: bytes, signature_header: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    values = dict(part.split("=", 1) for part in signature_header.split(","))
    try:
        timestamp = int(values["t"])
    except (KeyError, ValueError):
        return False
    if abs(time.time() - timestamp) > TOLERANCE_IN_SECONDS:
        return False
    signed_payload = f"{values['t']}.".encode() + raw_body
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode(), signed_payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, values.get("v1", ""))
```
